title: Debugging: Tracing & Verbose Output 🐛
description: Shine a light into your script with `set -x`, `-v`, and custom PS4 to track every step.

slides.title: When Scripts Go Wrong 🐞
slides.content:
## Time to Debug

Bash provides built‑in tracing tools that print each command before executing it. This is invaluable for understanding complex scripts.

- `set -x` – **xtrace**: print each command after expansion, preceded by `PS4`.
- `set -v` – **verbose**: print each command as written, before expansion.

These can be turned on/off for specific sections.

slides.title: Enable Tracing
slides.content: Activate with `set -x` and run a simple loop:
slides.codeSnippet:
set -x
for i in 1 2 3; do
  echo $i
done
set +x

quizData.question: What does `set +x` do?
quizData.explanation: Using `+` instead of `-` turns the option off.

slides.title: Customising the Trace with PS4 🎨
slides.content:
## Add Line Numbers and Timestamps

`PS4` is the prompt printed before each traced line. Default is `+`. Enhance it:

```bash
export PS4='+ $BASH_SOURCE:$LINENO: '
set -x
```
This shows the file name and line number, making it easy to locate the source of every action.

quizData.question: `set -v` prints commands after variable expansion and substitution.
quizData.explanation: `set -v` prints commands verbatim before expansion; `set -x` prints after expansion.

slides.title: Debugging a Section 🎯
slides.content:
## Wrap Only the Problematic Code

Instead of tracing the whole script, enable tracing just around the suspicious lines:
```bash
set -x
# code to debug
set +x
```
Or use `bash -x script.sh` to trace from the command line.

slides.title: Using `trap DEBUG` 🕵️
slides.content:
## Per‑Command Hooks

`trap 'commands' DEBUG` executes code before every simple command. Advanced users can use it to customise breakpoints, print variable values, or pause.

```bash
trap 'echo "About to run: $BASH_COMMAND"' DEBUG
```

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content: Combine `set -x` with redirection: `exec 2>/tmp/debug.log` and then enable xtrace – all trace output goes to the file.
